events.objective: Establish the precise onset and blast radius of the settlement incident. Using query_metrics and query_logs, determine: (1) the exact time settlement consumer lag started rising and when 'zero settlements processed' began, (2) whether there are rebalance events, consumer-group errors, deserialization errors, DB connection pool exhaustion, or thread/CPU saturation on settlement-service in that window, (3) whether the broker/topic metrics (produce rate, partition lag distribution, bytes in/out) show upstream starvation vs consumer-side stall, and (4) whether any other services consuming the same topic or feeding settlement-service show correlated anomalies before the reported onset. Report concrete timestamps and error signatures.

Enumerate everything that changed around the onset across ALL services, not just settlement-service. Using get_config_changes and get_deployments for the window 2026-05-12T07:00Z–09:59Z, list every deploy and config change with exact timestamps, specifically including the settlement-service consumer poll settings change, and flag any changes to upstream producers, the message broker, or downstream dependents of settlement-service. Then use get_service_dependencies to map settlement-service's upstream/downstream/shared dependencies, and search_historical_incidents for prior 'consumer lag stuck' / 'zero settlements processed' incidents and their root causes.

Correlate the change timeline from task b against the onset time and error signatures from task a. Determine which specific change (if any) temporally and causally aligns with lag onset: does the settlement-service consumer poll settings change precede onset and plausibly cause a rebalance/stall, or does it predate onset by enough that it is coincidental, or is there an upstream/broker/downstream change that better explains zero settlements? Use get_service_dependencies to verify whether any implicated component is shared across affected services and search_historical_incidents for matching signatures. State the single most likely root cause and the runner-up.

args.query: consumer lag stuck zero settlements processed

events.statement: Exactly two changes occurred in 2026-05-12T07:00Z–09:59Z across ALL services: a settlement-service config change of consumer.max.poll.records from 500 to 200 at 07:35:00Z (author m.das), and an order-service deploy dep-6010 v2.16.0 at 07:40:00Z. No other service changed anything.

The settlement-service consumer poll-settings change (cfg-3004, 07:35:00Z) preceded the order-service deploy (dep-6010, 07:40:00Z) by 5 minutes, and both preceded the 08:22Z incident report. The poll change is the earliest change in the window.

The order-service deploy changed the OrderExecuted event schema: field renamed qty -> quantity, added field 'venue', added an 'event schema version header v2'. order-service is an upstream producer of the events settlement-service consumes; dep-6010 status is 'live' and rolled_back_at is null.

settlement-service dependencies: consumes from kafka (queue-consume) and writes to ledger-db (db). Both kafka and ledger-db are marked shared:true and are owned by 'platform', not by the payments-owned settlement-service.

No config change or deploy was recorded for kafka or ledger-db on 2026-05-12 (kafka config count 0, kafka deploys count 0, ledger-db deploys count 0) — the broker and shared DB had no declared change in the window despite being shared components.

Two prior 'consumer lag growing / settlements stuck' incidents both cite kafka partition reassignment/rebalance as root cause (HIST-112 settlement-service 2026-02-03 'Consumer lost partition assignment during broker maintenance'; HIST-104 notification-service 2025-11-05 'Partition reassignment caused consumer group rebalancing storm') — these are leads only, not evidence about the current incident.

events.answer: Across ALL services in 07:00Z–09:59Z only two changes exist: settlement-service config cfg-3004 changed consumer.max.poll.records 500→200 at 07:35:00Z, and order-service deployed dep-6010 v2.16.0 at 07:40:00Z, which renames the consumed OrderExecuted field qty→quantity, adds 'venue', and adds an event schema version v2 header. The broker (kafka) and the shared ledger-db show zero deploys and zero config changes. settlement-service consumes from the shared kafka topic and writes to the shared ledger-db. The earliest change in the window is the consumer poll setting (07:35Z), 5 min before the order-service schema deploy (07:40Z); both precede the 08:22Z report. Historical precedents HIST-112/HIST-104 attribute similar lag symptoms to kafka partition reassignment, but those are leads only.

events.statement: Settlement consumer lag was at baseline (~26-55 messages, avg 31.06 at 07:40:00Z) through the 07:40Z bucket, then jumped to avg 603.29 / max 819.95 in the 07:42:00Z bucket — onset between 07:40 and 07:42.

The first ERROR on settlement-service in the window is a deserialization failure at 07:42:14Z: 'failed to deserialize OrderExecuted at orders-3@8841207: missing required field 'qty' (schema v1 expected, header says v2)'. This pattern fired 213 times (first_seen 07:42:14Z).

A second error pattern follows: 'poison message: retrying orders-3@8841207 (attempt <n>), partition blocked' (196 occurrences, first_seen 07:44:51Z) — the same offset 8841207 on partition orders-3 is retried indefinitely, which is the mechanism that stalls the partition.

Settlement lag grew monotonically and did not recover: from 603 (07:42) through 20,525 (08:25:34 avg, max 22062), 60,220.76 avg / max 61,605.53 at 09:55 — approximately 60k and climbing as reported. All 409 matched log lines in 07:00-09:59 were ERROR level.

No resource saturation or DB pool exhaustion on settlement-service: db_pool_in_use stayed flat at ~5.85-6.17 avg (max 6.78) across 160 points from 07:20 to 09:52, and cpu_pct rose from 28.68% avg (07:20) to ~69-71% avg (max 78.28%) and stayed there — elevated but not saturated.

No rebalance or connection-pool log events were found on settlement-service in 07:00-09:59: both the 'rebalance' and 'pool' searches returned total_matched 0. No consumer-group rebalance evidence in the log store.

order-service shows no error signal correlated with settlement onset: only 2 WARN lines in 07:00-09:59 — a connection-reset retry at 07:22:50Z and a slow /internal/metrics request at 09:14:44Z — neither coincides with the 07:42 onset.

Interpretation: the settlement stall is consumer-side and schema-driven — messages on topic 'orders' partition 3 are being produced with header schema v2 while the settlement consumer expects v1 ('header says v2'), so the consumer cannot deserialize offset 8841207 and blocks the whole partition. The growing lag is the blocked partition accumulating, not upstream produce failure. The reported 'consumer poll settings change' is not reflected in any rebalance/pool error in the logs.

No metric-based evidence that zero settlements were processed (a processed/settlements counter was not among available_metrics: consumer_lag, cpu_pct, db_pool_in_use, error_rate, latency_p99_ms, memory_pct, request_rate, restarts).

events.answer: Settlement consumer lag was normal (~30-55 messages) through the 07:40:00Z bucket, then jumped to 603 by the 07:42:00Z bucket — the first error is an ERROR at 07:42:14Z on settlement-service: "failed to deserialize OrderExecuted at orders-3@8841207: missing required field 'qty' (schema v1 expected, header says v2)". Lag then grew monotonically to ~60k by 09:55Z. The stall is consumer-side (poison-message partition block on orders-3), not upstream starvation or resource saturation: DB pool flat ~6 conns, CPU rose only to ~70%. No rebalance or pool-exhaustion events appeared.

events.statement: Re-query of ALL services 2026-05-12T07:00Z-09:59Z returns exactly one config change and one deployment: cfg-3004 settlement-service consumer.max.poll.records 500->200 at 07:35:00Z (author m.das, 'Smaller poll batches to smooth DB writes') and dep-6010 order-service v2.16.0 at 07:40:00Z. No other service changed anything; both precede the 08:22Z report.

Temporal alignment: the last normal lag bucket is 07:40Z (avg 31.06) and the first elevated bucket is 07:42Z (avg 603.29); dep-6010 deployed 07:40:00Z sits inside that gap, and the first deserialization ERROR is 07:42:14Z — i.e. the order-service deploy precedes the first failed offset by ~2 minutes, whereas the poll change precedes it by ~7 minutes.

The deploy's declared change set matches the error signature verbatim: dep-6010 changes are 'OrderExecuted event: rename field qty -> quantity', 'add field venue', 'event schema version header v2', and the first ERROR is 'missing required field qty (schema v1 expected, header says v2)' at offset orders-3@8841207. This is a genuine payload-contract break on the exact field/header named.

The consumer poll-settings change (cfg-3004, 500->200 max.poll.records) has no corresponding failure signature: T1 found no consumer-group rebalance and no pool events on settlement-service, and db_pool_in_use stayed flat ~5.85-6.17. A batch-size reduction cannot itself produce a schema/deserialization failure, so its 07:35Z position is timing-only, not mechanism.

Shared-component check: settlement-service depends on kafka (queue-consume) and ledger-db (db); both are shared:true and owned by 'platform', and neither had any deploy or config change on 2026-05-12 (broker/DB change counts zero). No change to the broker or shared DB competes as an explanation for the stall.

Historical leads do not match this incident's mechanism: HIST-112 (settlement-service 2026-02-03, 'Consumer lost partition assignment during broker maintenance') and HIST-104 (notification-service, 'Partition reassignment caused consumer group rebalancing storm') both cite kafka partition reassignment/rebalance, but T1 found zero rebalance events; a search for deserialization/schema-mismatch precedents returned 0 incidents. Both HIST hits are match_score-only leads, not evidence about the current incident.

events.description: No producer-side or schema-registry telemetry was retrieved to directly confirm order-service emitted v2-header OrderExecuted messages onto partition orders-3 at 07:40-07:42Z; the link rests on the deploy's declared change set vs the error text.

events.answer: The single most likely root cause is the order-service deploy dep-6010 (v2.16.0, 2026-05-12T07:40:00Z): it renames OrderExecuted qty->quantity and stamps a v2 schema header, so settlement-service (expecting schema v1) cannot deserialize offset orders-3@8841207; the record is retried as a poison message ('partition blocked') at 07:42:14Z and stops the partition, giving zero settlements and monotonically growing lag (603 -> 60,220). The reported settlement consumer poll-settings change (cfg-3004, 500->200 at 07:35:00Z) precedes onset by ~7 minutes but has NO matching error/rebalance signature and cannot cause a deserialization failure, so it is temporally coincidental rather than causal. Runner-up is a Kafka-side partition reassignment/rebalance (per HIST-112/HIST-104), disfavored because zero rebalance events were observed and the shared broker had no change.

tasks.objective: Establish the precise onset and blast radius of the settlement incident. Using query_metrics and query_logs, determine: (1) the exact time settlement consumer lag started rising and when 'zero settlements processed' began, (2) whether there are rebalance events, consumer-group errors, deserialization errors, DB connection pool exhaustion, or thread/CPU saturation on settlement-service in that window, (3) whether the broker/topic metrics (produce rate, partition lag distribution, bytes in/out) show upstream starvation vs consumer-side stall, and (4) whether any other services consuming the same topic or feeding settlement-service show correlated anomalies before the reported onset. Report concrete timestamps and error signatures.
tasks.answer: Settlement consumer lag was normal (~30-55 messages) through the 07:40:00Z bucket, then jumped to 603 by the 07:42:00Z bucket — the first error is an ERROR at 07:42:14Z on settlement-service: "failed to deserialize OrderExecuted at orders-3@8841207: missing required field 'qty' (schema v1 expected, header says v2)". Lag then grew monotonically to ~60k by 09:55Z. The stall is consumer-side (poison-message partition block on orders-3), not upstream starvation or resource saturation: DB pool flat ~6 conns, CPU rose only to ~70%. No rebalance or pool-exhaustion events appeared.

tasks.objective: Enumerate everything that changed around the onset across ALL services, not just settlement-service. Using get_config_changes and get_deployments for the window 2026-05-12T07:00Z–09:59Z, list every deploy and config change with exact timestamps, specifically including the settlement-service consumer poll settings change, and flag any changes to upstream producers, the message broker, or downstream dependents of settlement-service. Then use get_service_dependencies to map settlement-service's upstream/downstream/shared dependencies, and search_historical_incidents for prior 'consumer lag stuck' / 'zero settlements processed' incidents and their root causes.
tasks.answer: Across ALL services in 07:00Z–09:59Z only two changes exist: settlement-service config cfg-3004 changed consumer.max.poll.records 500→200 at 07:35:00Z, and order-service deployed dep-6010 v2.16.0 at 07:40:00Z, which renames the consumed OrderExecuted field qty→quantity, adds 'venue', and adds an event schema version v2 header. The broker (kafka) and the shared ledger-db show zero deploys and zero config changes. settlement-service consumes from the shared kafka topic and writes to the shared ledger-db. The earliest change in the window is the consumer poll setting (07:35Z), 5 min before the order-service schema deploy (07:40Z); both precede the 08:22Z report. Historical precedents HIST-112/HIST-104 attribute similar lag symptoms to kafka partition reassignment, but those are leads only.

tasks.objective: Correlate the change timeline from task b against the onset time and error signatures from task a. Determine which specific change (if any) temporally and causally aligns with lag onset: does the settlement-service consumer poll settings change precede onset and plausibly cause a rebalance/stall, or does it predate onset by enough that it is coincidental, or is there an upstream/broker/downstream change that better explains zero settlements? Use get_service_dependencies to verify whether any implicated component is shared across affected services and search_historical_incidents for matching signatures. State the single most likely root cause and the runner-up.
tasks.answer: The single most likely root cause is the order-service deploy dep-6010 (v2.16.0, 2026-05-12T07:40:00Z): it renames OrderExecuted qty->quantity and stamps a v2 schema header, so settlement-service (expecting schema v1) cannot deserialize offset orders-3@8841207; the record is retried as a poison message ('partition blocked') at 07:42:14Z and stops the partition, giving zero settlements and monotonically growing lag (603 -> 60,220). The reported settlement consumer poll-settings change (cfg-3004, 500->200 at 07:35:00Z) precedes onset by ~7 minutes but has NO matching error/rebalance signature and cannot cause a deserialization failure, so it is temporally coincidental rather than causal. Runner-up is a Kafka-side partition reassignment/rebalance (per HIST-112/HIST-104), disfavored because zero rebalance events were observed and the shared broker had no change.
